title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-08
lineage: SBD > (MR - Set 1, MC - Set 2) > C >D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a legendary late‑'69 run featuring a monster 27‑minute “Lovelight,” scorching “Dancin’ In The Streets,” and sublime renditions of “He Was A Friend Of Mine” and “New Potato Caboose.”
ai_review.review: The recording is an excellent soundboard source – listeners repeatedly note its crisp, pure fidelity with only a slight dip in quality after the mid‑set. Musically the show is hailed as one of the band’s peak performances: Jerry’s guitar work is described as spellbinding, the band locks into telepathic jams on “Dancin’” and “Lovelight,” and the acoustic beauty of “He Was A Friend Of Mine” shines throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed, mostly 5‑star reviews praise both the musical performance and the recording quality; the show is consistently called exceptional with only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly call the audio crisp, pure and crystal‑clear. One notes a slight degradation after the mid‑set (post “MAMU”), but overall the mix is balanced with no reported dropouts.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens with a blistering “Dancin’” that sets a high‑energy tone, flows into the epic “Lovelight” (featuring Wayne Ceballos), then moves through heartfelt acoustic moments (“He Was A Friend Of Mine”) and tight jams on “China Cat Sunflower” into a sublime “New Potato Caboose.” Guest Elvin Bishop adds color without disrupting the momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers hail his guitar solos as some of the best ever, note his vocal strength on “He Was A Friend Of Mine,” and praise his interplay with vocalist Wayne Ceballos during the 27‑minute “Lovelight.”
band_member_comments.Phil: A few mentions of a standout bass solo within “New Potato Caboose” and general admiration for the band’s telepathic listening, but no detailed critique of Phil’s playing.
